---
title: Chapters
description: Split a video into named chapters, written by an LLM from its transcript, and mark them on the player's time slider.
---

Chapters split a video into named parts, such as "Setting up" and
"Deploying", that the player marks on its time slider. ClipMux writes them
from the video's transcript with an LLM that the server's owner connected.
The model only picks where each chapter starts and names it; ClipMux works
out every time from the transcript itself.

<LeavesYourServers>
  Each time chapters are made, the video's transcript text is sent to the
  LLM provider the server's owner connected, such as OpenAI or Anthropic.
  No audio or video is sent. With a model on the owner's own network, such
  as Ollama, nothing leaves their machines.
</LeavesYourServers>

## Before you start

- An LLM connected on the ClipMux server, under **Captions & AI** in the
  dashboard. See [Choose an LLM for chapters](/docs/self-host/captions-and-ai/chapters-llm).
- An API key with `assets:write`, which the default scopes include.
- A video with speech. Chapters are made from its subtitles, so a video
  with no audio can't have them.

## Ask for chapters

### At upload

```ts title="app/api/clipmux/[action]/route.ts"
async upload(req, { file }) {
  return { passthrough: 'lesson_42', title: file.name, generate: { chapters: true } }
},
```

`generate: { chapters: true }` asks for subtitles too. Once the video is
ready, ClipMux transcribes it, then makes chapters from the transcript. If
no LLM is connected by then, the chapters track ends `errored` with
`llm_not_connected`; the video and its subtitles are unaffected.

### For a video you already have

```ts
const { track } = await clipmux.tracks.create('ast_…', { kind: 'chapters' })
```

`POST /v1/assets/{id}/tracks` with `{"kind": "chapters"}` answers `202`. A
video that has chapters keeps them until the new ones are ready. It
refuses with `409` and:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `subtitles_not_ready` | Chapters need ready subtitles. Ask for subtitles first, or wait for them. |
| `chapters_not_connected` | No LLM is connected for chapters on the server. |
| `asset_not_ready` | The video is still processing. |
| `job_active` | Another job is changing this video. Wait, or send `"supersede": true` to cancel a chapters job that's running. |

## What you get

A chapters track has `kind: "chapters"` and the same statuses and webhooks
as subtitles: `preparing`, then `ready` with `video.asset.track.ready`, or
`errored` with `video.asset.track.errored`.

- Between 1 and 10 chapters, as few as the content needs.
- Titles of up to 100 characters, on one line, in the transcript's
  language.
- The first chapter starts at 0, each one ends where the next starts, and
  the last ends at the end of the video.

Read them as JSON, in milliseconds, from the track:

```ts
const track = await clipmux.tracks.get('ast_…', 'trk_…')
// track.chapters: [{ start_ms: 0, end_ms: 95400, title: 'Setting up' }, …]
```

`GET /v1/assets/{id}/tracks/{track_id}` includes `chapters` once the track is
ready.

The same chapters are a WebVTT file, one numbered cue per chapter with its title
as the cue text, at the track's sidecar URL:

```txt
https://media.example.com/v/{token}/{playback_id}/tracks/{track_id}.vtt
```

```txt title="trk_….vtt"
WEBVTT
X-TIMESTAMP-MAP=MPEGTS:0,LOCAL:00:00:00.000

1
00:00:00.000 --> 00:01:35.400
Setting up

2
00:01:35.400 --> 00:04:12.000
Deploying
```

## Show them in the player

With `session-url`, `<clipmux-player>` finds the first ready chapters track
in the session and marks it on the time slider by itself. Otherwise, name
the track:

```html
<clipmux-player base-url="https://media.example.com" playback-id="pid_…" chapters-track="trk_…"></clipmux-player>
```

Chapters are never listed in the HLS playlist, so the player fetches the
VTT itself, with the playback token. When it has them, it fires
`clipmux-chapters` and sets `player.chapters`, in seconds:

```ts
player.addEventListener('clipmux-chapters', (e) => {
  for (const c of e.detail.chapters) console.log(c.startTime, c.endTime, c.title)
})
```

To list chapters in your own page or another player, fetch the VTT and read
it with `parseChapters` from `@clipmux/player`:

```ts
import { parseChapters } from '@clipmux/player'

const chapters = parseChapters(await (await fetch(vttUrl)).text())
// [{ startTime: 0, endTime: 95.4, title: 'Setting up' }, …]
```

## When chapters fail

An `errored` chapters track's `error_code` is one of:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `llm_not_connected` | No LLM is connected for chapters. Show nothing rather than an error; once the owner connects one, ask again with `POST /v1/assets/{id}/tracks`. |
| `subtitles_failed` | The subtitles chapters are made from failed. |
| `llm_unavailable` | The model kept failing, through three tries. |
| `model_rejected` | The provider refused the request. The owner should check the key and model. |
| `model_refused` | The model declined to write chapters for this transcript. |
| `invalid_model_output` | The model's chapters were still invalid after one corrective re-prompt. |
| `transcript_too_large` | The transcript makes a prompt over 512 KB. It is never cut short. |

Videos made before an LLM was connected don't get chapters by themselves:
ask for them again.

## Check it works

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/v1/assets/ast_…/tracks/trk_… \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY"
```

A `ready` track with a `chapters` list means it worked, and the player's
time slider shows the chapter marks. An `errored` track names its reason in
`error_code`, above.
